propers.text:
Largire nobis, quaesumus, Domine, semper spiritum cogitandi quae recta sunt,
propitius et agendi: ut, qui sine te esse non possumus, secundum te vivere
valeamus. Per Dominum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

NOTE for a reviewer: the 1570 reads 'conseruatione' where the 1962 and the 1862 and the 1604 all read 'conversatione'; the 1570 is used here only for largitate. provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 spells coeleste, 1962 caeleste (orthography); 1862 reads exequimur, 1962 exsequimur — one letter, the older against the modernised spelling of the same word. This is the only place in the lane where the two books differ inside a word other than by ae/oe or j/i, and it is recorded here plainly rather than smoothed away. CHECKED, not assumed: it is not an 1862 OCR dropout; 1862 prints cujus, 1962 cuius (j/i orthography); conclusion identical in both: the short cue 'Per Dominum.'; OCR damage in the 1862 layer, not textual: 'l)6minura' for Dominum (49263). Per dominum nostrum.' — with exequimur and celeste, i.e. agreeing with the 1862 on both points at issue. Every other occurrence of the word in the two degraded public-domain witnesses reads the same way: 1570 at lines 59562, 73316 and 73630, and Vatican typica 1604 at lines 43865, 44367 and 46509, all exequimur, none exsequimur.
